newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power firms on Maine nuclear outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power firms on Maine nuclear outage.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. firmed Thursday on the continued outage of the 910 megawatt (MW) Maine Yankee nuclear power station, traders said.
Limited spot supply from Canada also supported the next-day power values in the Northeast, they said.
"Canada has been stingy in sending power down," said a Northeast trader.
The Maine Yankee plant in Wiscasset, Maine, tripped off line Wednesday during testing. Maine Yankee officials have not announced the restart reschedule of the generating facility.

Peak, non-firm electricity for Friday delivery in New England Power Pool (NEPOOL) at the Northeast Utilities' territory border was valued near $33.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Wednesday's range of $31.00-$33.00.
Off-peak, non-firm NEPOOL power for Friday delivery at the NU border was quoted near $22.00, compared with a quote of $19.75-$22.00 on Wednesday.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPOOL), peak, non-firm power delivered in the western part of the grid for Friday was pegged near $19.00, up slightly from Wednesday's $18.75.
Off-peak, non-firm, western NYPP electricity for next-day delivery was valued at $14.00, compared with a range of $13.00-$14.00 on Wednesday.
For delivery Friday, peak non-firm power in eastern NYPP was assessed at $24.00-$27.00 a MWh, up from Wednesday's $22.00-$24.00.
Off-peak, non-firm eastern NYPP electricity for Friday was discussed at $18.50-$19.00, higher than a quote of $17.00-$18.00 on Wednesday.
